beats.text: Lea and Max each gave three hundred dollars to charity. Claimed separately, they get a hundred and sixteen dollars back. On one return: a hundred and forty-five.
Here's why. The federal donation credit is fourteen and a half percent on the first two hundred dollars. Above that, twenty-nine percent.
Claimed separately, each return uses up its own low-rate two hundred. Twice.
Combined, six hundred dollars on one return: two hundred at the low rate, four hundred at the high one. Twenty-nine dollars more, from the same gifts.
The twist: you can also hold small donations and claim them in any of the next five years, so a quiet year can join a bigger one.
So pool the receipts on one return, and check that spouse has enough tax to use the credit.
Next: moving for work or school, and which expenses count. Follow so you don't miss it.
